answer: Because the harbor hash is checked against the wander checkpoint at intake, the voyage audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 127 aliases cost 150 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
